newsitem.title: USA: Pepsi U.S. bottlers may expand overseas - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Pepsi U.S. bottlers may expand overseas - WSJ.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc is in talks that could let some of its U.S. bottlers invest in and take operating control of some of its international franchise territories, the Wall Street Journal reported Friday.
People familiar with the talks told the paper the discussions are preliminary and no decisions have been made.
Pepsi's international beverage business had an $846 million operating loss last year after charges, and this month the company said it expects a net loss of $25-$50 million in the division in 1997.

Friday's report said Pepsi bottlers believe a move to let Pepsi's strong U.S. bottlers expand overseas could create five or six large regional bottlers worldwide, a strategy that Coca-Cola has used successfully.

The report said the Whitman Corp's Pepsi-Cola General Bottlers unit, which is the second largest domestic Pepsi bottler after Pepsi's own bottling operations, is a likely candidate for acquiring more international territories.
A spokesman for Whitman told the paper the company has had "preliminary discussions" with Pepsi about acquiring more franchises.
